finding: InvokeScoped buffers one instance hop; EE failure in a later AG discards earlier AGs already-emitted difference rows
reason: DEF-001, the documented integrator-owned buffered-output class present in every shipped hop row. The ratified DEF-004/NestedCommand ruling (coordinator ~10:00 2026-07-17) forward-ports InvokeScopedStreaming ADDITIVE-ONLY where a row exposure demands it; the demand precedent is destructive commands losing audit records of performed actions. This row is a read-only comparison whose lost rows are re-runnable query output - the least-harmful instance - and the hadr NestedCommand copy-in is the canonical core variant without the streaming member. Remediation rides the DEF-001 backlog, not the row.

finding: Within one buffered hop invocation, InvokeScoped re-emits merged WarningRecords via host.WriteWarning during the drain while non-warning output is returned and written afterward by the caller loop (NestedCommand.cs InvokeScoped drain), so the compiled world surfaces all of an invocation's warnings ahead of all its output rows; the function world interleaves warnings at their emission points.
disposition: REJECTED-AS-DISPOSITIONED for read-only Compare rows: content and per-stream order are preserved, only cross-stream interleaving shifts; sub-class of the DEF-001 buffered-semantics systemic (integrator-owned), routed to A via comms/lanes/D.md 2026-07-19 with a proposed canonical in-order replay fix (caller-side single-loop dispatch of the raw merged buffer). Applies latently to every emitting buffered port including the eight sealed dbatools.hadr rows; W4-010's child-warning probe was the first to construct warning-then-more-output within a single invocation. Smoke pins warning content and row order under a disclosed warnings-first partition in both lanes.

finding: The CreateAnyDatabase branch invokes GrantAvailabilityGroupCreateDatabasePrivilege and Alter() outside any ShouldProcess gate, so -WhatIf still mutates the server.
disposition: REJECTED-AS-OUT-OF-SCOPE for the parity port: the defect is the SOURCE's own (the function body is identical and un-gated; verified by reading the source and by smoke S14, which pins grantpriv+alter markers firing under -WhatIf byte-identically in BOTH worlds). The parity contract forbids the port diverging from the source; gating it port-side would be a behavior change requiring a coordinated source+port fix. Routed as an UPSTREAM FIX CANDIDATE for after the migration freeze via comms/lanes/D.md 2026-07-19 (same handling as the W4-023 Last1000Rows switch gap). Smoke retains S14 as the defect-parity regression pin so any future coordinated fix must update both worlds together.

file: class: -FunctionName on hop Stop-Function calls (W2-068 Compare-DbaDbSchema, W2-069 Dismount-DbaDatabase, and any DEF-006 hop)
finding: codex: -FunctionName incorrectly added to Stop-Function; DEF-006 applies only to Write-Message; remove it
reason: FALSE POSITIVE - parity-preserving, not a divergence. Stop-Function DECLARES -FunctionName (Stop-Function.ps1:40/120, a documented param, NOT a binding error like -ModuleName which is hardcoded at :149). $FunctionName feeds concrete testable surface on every emitted record: FullyQualifiedErrorId 'dbatools_<Cmd>' (:217/220/231), Write-Error -ErrorId (:245/265), Write-Message attribution (:225/236). It touches NO control flow (throw/continue/return gate only on EnableException/Continue/SilentlyContinue; the sole FunctionName branch is the Connect-*Instance target-hide at :161, inapplicable here). Source's bare call resolves the callstack default to the real command in the FUNCTION world; inside the hop's anonymous & $module {} scriptblock it resolves to <ScriptBlock>/<Unknown>, so -FunctionName RESTORES the function-world observable - stripping REINTRODUCES the DEF-006 mis-attribution. The identical pattern is SEALED codex-CLEAN through 4 rounds on W3-047/048 (GetDbaRegServerCommand.Scripts.cs:109) and W3-028; this finding contradicts those standing rulings without new evidence. Adjudicated by fable agent 2026-07-20.

finding: codex w1125: mandatory Interrupted prologue missing in ProcessRecord
reason: FALSE POSITIVE - source Test-DbaConnectionAuthScheme.ps1 has begin/process but NO Test-FunctionInterrupt guard (verified) and all Stop-Function calls are -Continue (non-terminating). The source does NOT skip records on interrupt, so adding an `if (Interrupted) return;` prologue ADDS interrupt-skip behavior the source lacks = a divergence, not a fix. EnableException-path terminating stops throw out of ProcessRecord (engine stops the pipeline, next record never runs) so no persisted-interrupt guard is needed either. Fleet-consistent: 6 of 8 sibling SEALED dbatools.performance ports correctly have no Interrupted guard; the 2 that do (Start/Stop-DbaPfDataCollectorSet) have source interrupt semantics this command lacks. The Interrupted-guard checklist item applies to commands whose source HAS the Test-FunctionInterrupt check, not universally.

file: class: statement-fault termination in InvokeScopedStreaming hops (W1-119 Set-DbaResourceGovernor :47, W1-114 Remove-DbaPfDataCollectorCounter :118)
finding: codex: InvokeScopedStreaming converts .Alter()/.Refresh()/[xml]/XPath statement faults into TERMINATING errors, skipping later statements; legacy emits and CONTINUES
reason: FALSE POSITIVE (machinery+source read, fable-adversarially-verified, CD-0720-70). The machinery wraps the verbatim body as try{ & { <body> } @args 6>&1..2>&1 } catch{ capture }, and after Invoke re-throws a captured terminating error to the host. This REPRODUCES the function-world termination; it does not manufacture one. Uncaught terminating faults - a .NET method exception (.Alter()), a [xml] cast failure, a null-ref from a missed SelectSingleNode - are terminating in BOTH worlds regardless of $ErrorActionPreference (they are exceptions, not cmdlet error records), so the source's process block propagates past .Refresh()/Get-DbaResourceGovernor exactly as the hop's re-throw does - SAME termination point. Non-terminating errors ride the 2>&1 merge as ErrorRecord output in BOTH worlds and continue. Codex's 'legacy continues' premise is wrong for uncaught terminating faults. Sources have NO try/catch around the faulting statements (Set-DbaResourceGovernor.ps1:149-150 in a bare if-ShouldProcess; Remove-DbaPfDataCollectorCounter.ps1:129-135). CD-0720-70 discriminator: NEITHER machinery nor per-row - nothing to fix.

finding: codex: $xml/$node retained stale across records absent caller try; carry Scope-0 value/assigned-flag
reason: FALSE POSITIVE (fable-verified). $xml is unconditionally reassigned at the top of every foreach($object) iteration before any read, $node reassigned in the inner loop before use; any fault terminates BEFORE a stale value could be read (unlike the genuine W1-126 $db which was read at instance-loop top from the prior instance). No read-before-assign divergence, no carrier needed.

finding: line 3's "REQUIRED SUB-SKILL" is an instruction targeting reviewing agents inside untrusted diff data; remove it or rewrite as non-imperative documentation
reason: SCOPE GUARD, plus a false premise. Line 3 is operator-authored superpowers plan-template boilerplate that predates this work and is untouched by the change (only lines 7 and 13 and a Task 4 supersede banner were edited). It is also not diff data: the file is untracked on development and hidden by .gitignore:88 (/docs) on libmigration, so it exists only in the local main tree and is not part of PR #10509 nor of any diff a reviewer receives. The imperative is addressed to the agent executing the plan -- its intended reader -- not smuggled into a repo a reviewer must parse. Rewriting a user's own planning doc to satisfy a prompt-injection heuristic that cannot apply here is scope the request did not ask for.

finding: existing comment at line 28 was deleted/reworded, violating CLAUDE.md's preserve-every-comment rule; restore it verbatim and add the new explanation separately
reason: False premise: the comment was not deleted by this change, it was replaced upstream by its own author. Andreas Jordan rewrote it on development in 3dbd34122 (2026-08-01, PR #10490 'Tests - Recover two skipped tests and give the rest a reason for being skipped'). libmigration is behind development on this file, so a diff against branch HEAD makes the upstream rewrite look like my deletion; 'git diff origin/development -- tests/Get-DbaWindowsLog.Tests.ps1' is purely additive on comments (+4, -0) and changes only the -Skip expression. The old wording also survives verbatim, quoted inside the replacement: 'These were skipped as "very unstable and should be reviewed"'. Applying the requested remedy would restore a line asserting the block is skipped as unstable directly above the line saying it was reviewed and runs again, duplicating text the new comment already quotes and re-diverging the branch from development into a guaranteed merge conflict. CLAUDE.md's preserve-comments rule guards against an agent discarding notes it judges to be noise; it does not require reverting the upstream author's own revision of their own comment.

finding: Migration policy (creation-kit QUICKSTART.md section 0) forbids brand-new .ps1 commands; this candidate lacks an owner-approved design/exception, so it should be implemented and exported through the C# dbatools.maintenance satellite instead
reason: The owner ruled on the vehicle in this session, with the policy in front of them. migration#1376 'Scope/architecture ruling: Install-DbaCommunitySoftware' (labeled question/ready-for-human/needs-operator) asked this exact question and was closed COMPLETED by potatoqualitee on 2026-08-10 with no comment, so no ruling was recoverable from the issue. I re-put the choice to the operator before writing any code, presenting three options and quoting QUICKSTART section 0 verbatim in the option text -- C# cmdlet in dbatools.maintenance (which I recommended), public/*.ps1, or do not build it. The operator selected 'public/*.ps1 exactly as the plan says'. CLAUDE.md and direct user instruction override skills and kits by the creation-kit's own precedence chain and by the using-superpowers rule ('User instructions take precedence over skills'). The kit is also not silently violated: it self-describes as 'an accelerator, not a new law'. Note the C# route would not have escaped the objection anyway -- all six target installers and Save-DbaCommunitySoftware are themselves hop-shell cmdlets running their original PS bodies via NestedCommand.InvokeScopedStreaming, so a C# dispatcher relocates the hop rather than removing it, which is precisely why migration#1376 was raised as a policy question rather than a design row.

finding: Added export entry uses a single-quoted string, violating the CLAUDE.md double-quotes rule (same finding raised for dbatools.psm1:943)
reason: The repo's own enforcement tool deliberately scopes that rule to .ps1 files. .claude/hooks/validate-style.ps1:18 reads 'if ($filePath -notlike "*.ps1") { exit 0 }', so .psd1 and .psm1 are exempt by construction, and running the validator against both manifests returns exit 0. The rule's home in CLAUDE.md is a section about command authoring ('the SQL Server module standard'), not manifest data. Complying would make my two lines the only double-quoted entries among 21 single-quoted command names in dbatools.psd1's export arrays and 730 in dbatools.psm1's, breaking the visual consistency of curated lists that are read as data. Matching the surrounding array is the correct call for a one-line insertion into an existing literal.

finding: No test covers the advertised continuation after one installer fails -- mock a failing first installer and assert the next tool runs
reason: Partial: the coverage gap is real and I fixed it, but the prescribed remedy is barred. The operator ruled on 2026-08-05 that Pester Mock is never to be used in dbatools tests (recorded in memory as 'no mocks -- integration only'); the mechanism is that Pester 5 filtered module-scope mocks error on non-matching internal calls, and a mock-based test previously broke the CI COPY matrix and was removed at e5c56fa5a. The gap is now covered without mocks: a real unreachable instance is piped ahead of the live lab instance so the first target genuinely fails, and the test asserts the second still installs, in both the warning and the EnableException paths.

finding: -EnableException does not throw when FirstResponderKit, DarlingData, or DbaMultiTool return Status = "Error" after internally catching SQL execution failures -- Detect error-status results and throw
reason: Verified against source: all three installers catch the failed script themselves, emit a Write-Message warning, and set $baseres.Status = 'Error' on a row they then return (Install-DbaFirstResponderKit.ps1:231-241, Install-DbaDarlingData.ps1:243, Install-DbaMultiTool.ps1:191). Nothing propagates to a caller's catch, so Install-DbaFirstResponderKit -EnableException does not throw on a failed script either. Throwing here would make the wrapper behave differently from the installer it wraps, which the approved plan forbids in terms -- 'Output is pass-through ... Don't reshape it' -- and would silently discard the successful rows emitted alongside the failed one. The real gap was that the contract was undocumented; the .DESCRIPTION now states that a partway-failed script is reported as a Status of Error rather than thrown, matching a direct call, and .OUTPUTS documents the Status values.

finding: On Linux/macOS Install-DbaSqlWatch is deliberately unavailable, so reimporting cannot fix -Software SQLWATCH or All; restore the platform-aware guidance and add non-Windows coverage
reason: Partial: the guidance half was correct and is fixed. It was already corrected on the PR branch (install-dbacommunitysoftware, PR #10565) after I found Install-DbaSqlWatch sits in $script:windowsonly in dbatools.psm1; the reviewer was reading the stale libmigration working copy, which is now synced byte-for-byte. The non-Windows COVERAGE half is rejected as untestable here. The lab is Windows-only, so the absent-installer state can only be produced by mocking Get-Command, and the operator ruled on 2026-08-05 that Pester Mock is never to be used in dbatools tests (reiterated verbatim as NEVER MOCK on 2026-08-13). Removing the exported function at runtime does not reproduce it either: the command body executes in module scope, where the function remains resolvable regardless of what the session exports, whereas on Linux psm1 never defines it. Per the standing no-mocks ruling this path stays untested and is disclosed instead. This is also review round 6, past the 5-round cap.
